request: Our school library wants a simple catalogue of its books. The librarian should be able to add a book with its title, its author and how many copies the library owns. Students should be able to see all the books, and look at one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name, and returns it when they are done; a student can only return a book they actually borrowed. When every copy of a book is out, nobody else can borrow it until a copy comes back.
summary:
I've built the library catalogue in `app.py`, and all 6 of my tests pass. It saves everything in a file called `library.db` in the project folder, and creates its tables when the app starts. Every answer comes back as JSON.

**What it can do**

| Action | Request | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Librarian adds a book | `POST /books` with `{"title", "author", "copies"}` | Saves the book. Title and author can't be blank, and the library must own at least 1 copy. |
| Students see all books | `GET /books` | Lists every book with how many copies the library owns and how many are on the shelf now. |
| Students look at one book | `GET /books/{id}` | Shows that book, including copies on the shelf. Gives a "not found" error if the book doesn't exist. |
| Borrow a book | `POST /books/{id}/borrow` with `{"student_name"}` | Records the loan and takes one copy off the shelf. Refused if every copy is out. |
| Return a book | `POST /books/{id}/return` with `{"student_name"}` | Records the return and puts one copy back. Refused if that student doesn't currently have the book out. |

**Rules you asked for**
- **No borrowing when every copy is out:** the request is refused until someone returns a copy. If two students try to take the last copy at the same moment, only one gets it.
- **Students can only return what they borrowed:** returning a book you never borrowed, or returning the same copy twice, is refused.

**Things to know**
- **Borrowing more than once:** you didn't say whether a student can borrow several copies of the same book, so it's allowed for now.
- **Names identify students:** there are no logins. Each student is just the name they type, so two students with the same name would count as one person. It also means anyone can return a book by typing the borrower's name.
- **Anyone can add books:** nothing checks that the person adding a book is really the librarian.
- **Test data:** the tests write to the same `library.db`, so you might want to delete that file before the library starts using the app.
